lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Picture a classroom full of laptops where, by the end of the night, everybody owns a brand new cryptocurrency they made themselves. And they're sending it to each other.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wait, they invented their own money? In one evening?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A token, yes, on a test network, so nothing real is at stake. It was Byzantium's first Ethereum workshop, held on the eleventh of March, 2024, at ÉTS. Khalil Anis Zabat led and organized it, and Antoine wrote the recap.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Beginners and more advanced people in the same room. How do you teach that without losing half of them?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The arc was deliberate. First, Remix, which runs in the browser, so nobody needed a full toolchain installed and they could redo everything at home. Then a local dev setup, the way professionals repeat the process.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sepolia, a test network. Test ETH from a faucet, MetaMask as the wallet, and a service like Infura as the bridge to the chain. Then the key trick: don't rewrite the basics. They used OpenZeppelin, a shared library of battle-tested standards, and inherited an ERC-20 token.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So what do you actually have to write?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hardly anything. A name, a symbol, the decimals, often eighteen, and an initial amount minted to whoever deploys the contract. That's the whole starting point Khalil walked through.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Everyone deployed, copied their contract addresses, and sent tokens to each other until the room felt like a tiny economy. Antoine's line sums it up: until you push a transaction and see it on a block explorer, Solidity is just syntax. Afterward it's a public ledger with your address on one line.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Questions about gas, since infinite loops can burn it and stall a contract. About the ABI, which tells apps which functions exist. And about why big data stays off-chain, with only a hash or a link on the chain.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, other token types and more advanced techniques. The full write-up has photos from the room and the starting contract code.
